purpose: Algorithm used in emergency departments to prioritize patients by acuity and anticipated resource needs, not just diagnosis.

levels.name: Resuscitation
levels.criteria: Requires immediate lifesaving intervention: unresponsive/cannot follow commands, ineffective airway, SpO2 < 90% with respiratory compromise, hemodynamic instability with hypoperfusion, severe brady/tachycardia, or cardiac/pulmonary arrest.

levels.name: Emergent
levels.criteria: High-risk situation (threat to life, limb, sight, or organ function), acute change in mental status, or severe pain/distress (>=7/10). Examples: possible ACS, stroke symptoms, severe hemorrhage, suicidal/homicidal ideation.

levels.name: Urgent
levels.criteria: Stable, but needs two or more different resource types to reach a disposition (e.g. labs, imaging, IV fluids, specialty consult).

levels.name: Less Urgent
levels.criteria: Stable, needs exactly one resource (e.g. a single lab test, a simple wound repair).

levels.name: Non-Urgent
levels.criteria: Stable, needs no resources (e.g. prescription refill, immunization only).

vital_sign_uptriage: For an ESI-3 adult patient, danger-zone vital signs (heart rate > 100, respiratory rate > 20, SpO2 < 92%) should prompt consideration of uptriage to ESI-2, accounting for medications and chronic conditions that can blunt compensatory responses.

_sources.title: Emergency Severity Index Handbook, 5th Edition (Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality / ACEP)
